user_input: Which PowerFlex 520 digital input selections relate to auxiliary fault, clear fault, and ramp stop?
reference_answer: Selection 12 "Aux Fault" causes an F002 Auxiliary Input fault when the input is removed. Selection 13 "Clear Fault" clears an active fault when active. Selection 14 "RampStop,CF" causes the drive to ramp to a stop regardless of P045 Stop Mode.

reference_evidence.quote:
12 “Aux Fault” When enabled, an F002 “Auxiliary Input” fault occurs when the input is removed.
13 “Clear Fault” When active, clears an active fault.
14 “RampStop,CF” Causes drive to immediately ramp to a stop regardless of how P045
[Stop Mode] is set.

user_input: Why is a properly performed Auto Tune important on a PowerFlex 520-series drive?
reference_answer: A properly tested motor and drive helps ensure higher starting torque and better low-speed performance. An improperly performed Auto Tune can cause low-speed instability, uneven performance through the speed range, and unnecessary overcurrent or overvoltage faults.

reference_evidence.quote:
A properly tested motor and drive helps ensure higher starting torque and
better performance at low speeds. Conversely, an improperly performed Auto
Tune can cause the motor to exhibit instability at low speeds, uneven
performances when running through the motor speed range, and can generate
unnecessary faults such as overcurrent and overvoltage faults.

user_input: How do you acknowledge a motion control error with MC_Reset on an S7-1200 PLC?

reference_evidence.quote:
To acknowledge an error with MC_Reset, follow these steps:
1. Check the requirements indicated above.
2. Start the acknowledgement of the error with a rising edge at the Execute input parameter.
3. The error has been acknowledged when Done equals TRUE and the technology object
tag <Axis name>.StatusBits.Error equals FALSE.
